Outcome: Depressive symptoms (lower is better)

## Study A
Found: benefit
Claim: Higher serum 25(OH)D3 at age 9.8 was associated with lower depressive symptoms at age 13.8.
Sentence: "Higher concentrations of 25(OH)D(3) assessed at mean age 9.8 years were associated with lower levels of depressive symptoms at age 13.8 years [adjusted risk ratio (RR; 95% confidence interval (CI)): 0.90 (0.86-0.95)], but not at age 10.6 years [adjusted RR (95% CI): 0.98 (0.93-1.03)] and with increased odds of decreasing symptoms between age 10.6 and 13.8 years [adjusted RR (95% CI): 1.08 (1.01-1.16)]."
Measured as: depressive symptoms (Mood and Feelings Questionnaire) at age 13.8
Population: Children from a prospective cohort, mean age 9.8 years at vitamin D measurement
Intervention: Serum 25(OH)D3 concentration (measured, not given)
Comparator: Lower 25(OH)D3 concentrations
Design: cohort study
Sample size: not reported
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

## Study B
Found: no effect
Claim: Depression severity was not correlated with serum vitamin D concentration in postmenopausal women.
Sentence: "No correlation of the depression severity with the serum vitamin D concentration or other criteria of metabolic syndrome was found."
Measured as: depression severity (Beck Depression Inventory)
Population: 396 postmenopausal women from rural and urban areas in the Lublin region, Poland
Intervention: Serum vitamin D concentration (measured, not administered)
Comparator: Lower vs higher serum vitamin D levels across participants
Design: cross-sectional study
Sample size: 396
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported
